clue.text: A raptor or two produces ecstasy — we all go mad

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: going mad suggests the words we all go are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a dose of ecstasy will send the whole party crazy, with birds of prey thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges WE ALL GO into AGLEOWL after E. The definition is witty: the bird's name is itself two raptors, an eagle and an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: This large bird of prey is a raptor whose name joins the names of two other raptors.

clue.text: Houses in forest at Epping

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Homes have been built in Epping Forest, near London.
explanation.walkthrough: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the edge of London. 'Houses' is a collective plural: an estate is a group of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned group of houses built together.

clue.text: Speedy butchers need good cutter

parts.note: a lance is a surgical blade, a cutter

explanation.surface: Fast-working butchers require a sharp knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. So a speedy butcher's is a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look is a glance, and in rhyming slang a butcher's is a look.

clue.text: Film about light: one thousand sheep, for example, desirable extra concept in which I tell it afresh in old king Cole's words

indicators.note: the film title goes about, that is round, the word for light

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
a Very light is a coloured signal flare
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a ewe is a female sheep
say means for example
good means desirable
in cricket a bye is an extra, a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: in which means the following letter goes inside the word for concept

parts.note: an idea is a concept

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the letters of the two words are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A rambling description of a film full of sheep and ideas, retold in a nursery-rhyme king's voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VERY in ET; 'in which' puts I into IDEA; 'afresh' rearranges TELL IT. The whole is a Cole Porter song title, the theme hinted at by 'old king Cole'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous Cole Porter song, so it is literally words written by Cole.

clue.text: See 3
Call from the pink for return of some US unions in the blue

indicators.note: a return sends the whole assembled run back the way it came, so it reads from the end
the union letters sit inside the word for the blue

parts.note: the blue is a poetic name for the sky
the CIO, the Congress of Industrial Organizations, was a federation of American unions

explanation.surface: A huntsman's call somehow linked to American trade unions coming back into the open sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'return of' turns the whole assembled container backwards. 'The pink' is the scarlet coat worn for fox hunting, so a call from the pink is a hunting cry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional cry of fox hunters urging on hounds, and hunters wear the scarlet coat called pink.

clue.text: Topless dance has pleasant smell

indicators.note: topless means losing its top, so the first letter of the dance is removed

parts.note: the morris is a traditional English folk dance

explanation.surface: A topless dance comes with a nice scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance done with bells and sticks; without its first letter M it leaves ORRIS. The surface suggests a racy show.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root, from the iris, has a violet-like fragrance used in perfumes, so it stands for a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Unassailable study about being on the move

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for study goes round the other piece

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
astir means up and about, moving

explanation.surface: A thesis is unbeatable when it concerns things in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'con' is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart, which the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron case or alibi is one so solid it cannot be attacked or broken.

clue.text: Grasses in footwear

definitions.meaning: a grass is an informer, so grasses are people who tell tales

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer. 'in' is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who sneak are informers, and the word also names soft-soled sports shoes.

clue.text: Cross between painting (with backing) and poetry

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for painting is read in reverse

parts.note: painting is a form of art
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hybrid of a backed canvas and a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' signals the reversal. 'Cross between' reads like a hybrid, but 'Cross' alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a place is to go across it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Ship's company thus reported one who left it

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew, and thus is so

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is mentioned, along with a sailor who abandoned it.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinson Crusoe, the novel's hero, left his ship and ended up a castaway; 'crew so' said out loud gives his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero Robinson Crusoe went to sea and was the lone survivor who left the wrecked vessel.

clue.text: Holiday finished with significant discovery

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
through means finished, as in I am through with it

explanation.surface: A holiday is over and something important has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is an important advance or discovery, especially in science.

clue.text: Vulgar and somewhat adhesive …

definitions.meaning: vulgar here means cheap and in poor taste
slightly sticky, as paint that has not fully dried

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tasteless and cheap, and slightly sticky to the touch, two separate senses.

clue.text: … doctor is possible criterion

annotationWithheld.why: '… doctor is possible criterion': the anagram fodder is the previous answer (TACKY), carried over by the ellipsis, plus DR and IS; no word of this clue gives TACKY, so the parse cannot be quoted from the clue as held

clue.text: Unit of energy on first base at old solver among kings

indicators.note: the middle pieces are placed among the two royal letters, which go outside them

parts.note: K and R are both abbreviations for king, K from chess and R from Rex
I is the Roman numeral one, as in first
base means low, as in base instincts
the solver is addressed as you, and thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An energy unit is explained in terms of baseball bases and an old puzzler sitting among royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts ILOWATTHOU between K and R. Addressing the solver as 'you' is a crossword convention, so 'old solver' is the archaic THOU.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a measure of energy, a thousand watts sustained for sixty minutes, used on electricity bills.

clue.text: Cheating couple with use of stopwatch?

parts.note: a couple is two
using a stopwatch is timing something

explanation.surface: A pair are being unfaithful, with a stopwatch involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing means being unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else.

clue.text: A majority of Juliet's family have company in American resort

indicators.note: taking the majority of the name means keeping most of it and dropping the last letters

parts.note: Juliet in Romeo and Juliet belongs to the Capulet family

explanation.surface: Most of Juliet's relatives have guests over at a resort in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' trims CAPULET to CAPUL. 'American' is used in the wider sense: the resort is on Mexico's Pacific coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a famous beach resort city on the Pacific coast of Mexico, in North America.

clue.text: Ex-professor rues time wasted

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined or spoilt, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A retired academic regrets the time he squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeritus professor is one retired but keeping the title as an honour.

clue.text: The last at first amid vulgar praise

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the other pieces are placed inside the word for vulgar

parts.note: common means vulgar or low-class
the last of something is its end
I is the Roman numeral one, as in first

explanation.surface: Someone praises a person who came last at first, among the vulgar crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' signals the container, and the word for vulgar is split after its fourth letter. 'The last at first' reads like an order instruction but is just three pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A commendation is an expression of praise or approval, a noun synonym.

clue.text: 24 (note time)

definitions.meaning: the cross-reference points to the song's final word, meaning small
a note here is a written record, as of a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides two more meanings: as an adjective the word means tiny, and as a noun it is both a record of a meeting and a span of sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute means tiny, the minutes of a meeting are its notes, and a minute is sixty seconds.

clue.text: Holiday appeal

definitions.meaning: the first of May, a public holiday in many countries
a radio distress call asking for help

explanation.definitionFit: May Day is a spring festival, and the international distress signal sounds like the same words.

clue.text: Painter of light held by old king Cole

indicators.note: something held by another is inside it, so the beam goes within the songwriter's surname

parts.note: Cole Porter, the American songwriter, whose first name recalls the nursery rhyme's Old King Cole
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An artist of light is in the grip of the jolly monarch of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' signals the container. Old King Cole is a nursery rhyme figure; here 'Cole' leads to the songwriter Cole Porter, the theme of the long linked answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who portrays depicts things in pictures or words, so a painter is one kind of portrayer.

clue.text: Dominated with lines

definitions.meaning: marked with straight lines, as writing paper is

explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to govern, and ruled paper is printed with lines for writing.

clue.text: See 3
See 3
Cubic man spoken and translated as red

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the inventor's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Erno Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube puzzle, so he is the cubic man
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A cube-shaped man is described in speech and in translation as being red.
explanation.walkthrough: The inventor of the famous cube puzzle, Rubik, sounds the same spelt with a C; then 'and' put into German gives UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubicund means ruddy or reddish, used especially of a healthy or flushed face.

clue.text: Correctly positioned for the pull shot?

definitions.meaning: not offside, legitimately placed in football or rugby
in cricket the pull is played to the leg or ... of the field

explanation.definitionFit: The term means not offside in football, and in cricket names the leg side where pulls go.

clue.text: Thank you initially for embracing embracer with brutal violence

indicators.note: the two first letters go round the word for one who embraces, holding it
initially means at the start, so the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: a hugger is one who embraces

explanation.surface: A thank-you for being hugged is accompanied by savage violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T and Y from Thank and you, and 'embracing' puts them round HUGGER. 'embracing embracer' is a playful repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is the behaviour of thugs, that is violent and brutal conduct.
